docs_howvoting_p1: Anyone in the company can vote for solutions on an open challenge: one vote per solution, which can be withdrawn until the round closes. Votes are public.
docs_howvoting_p2: The most-voted solution at close goes to IT for release; ties go to the earliest submission. Vote for what would save time — no technical knowledge needed.
docs_goodvote_p1: Vote for the solution you would actually use, not the most impressive demo. Use “Run this solution” to test it; a short test says more than the title.
docs_goodvote_p2: Prefer solutions that are clear about their limits. A narrow tool that works reliably beats a broad one that almost works.
docs_writingchallenge_p1: Describe a real, recurring task in one or two sentences, and what “done” looks like — not how to build it. Start with the problem and the desired outcome.
docs_writingchallenge_p2: Attach realistic, safe sample input so builders can test against it. Keep the scope small; focused challenges attract more solutions.
docs_samplepolicy_p1: Challenges and solutions run on sample data, never on production systems. Add a representative extract under Sample data and mark personal data so it is hidden before any run.
docs_samplepolicy_p2: Policies set by the platform team, such as permitted AI models and external network access, apply to every run. A blocked run names the policy concerned.
docs_aftervoting_p1: When a round closes, the winning solution is announced and handed to IT for review, hardening and release. Progress is shown under Results.
docs_aftervoting_p2: Other solutions remain in the library as building blocks that anyone can reuse for the next challenge.
docs_sandbox_p1: Each builder has a private test environment, separate from colleagues’ work and from production systems. It starts on the first run and pauses when idle.
docs_sandbox_p2: Runs count towards the daily and weekly usage limits shown under Usage. A paused environment can be resumed; no work is lost.
docs_buildingblocks_p1: Building blocks are reusable steps — data sources, AI steps, logic and outputs — placed on the canvas. Each block declares its inputs and outputs, so only compatible blocks connect.
docs_buildingblocks_p2: Blocks are versioned, tested and published, so flows are assembled rather than programmed. New blocks can be created, tested and published for everyone.
docs_vibecoding_p1: Describe the goal in plain language and the AI assistant finds, adds, connects and configures blocks on the canvas. Every step is visible, metered and audited.
docs_vibecoding_p2: Use the assistant to set up a flow quickly, then refine it by hand. Without a configured AI provider, a basic built-in assistant is used.
docs_submitting_p1: When the flow works, name it, run it once more, and choose Submit as solution. It is linked to the challenge and opens for voting immediately.
docs_submitting_p2: State clearly what the solution does and where it stops. It can still be improved after submitting; version history restores any earlier state.

policy_desc_models_work_tiers: Which model each work tier (small / medium / large) resolves to. Nothing in Common Practice reads this setting today.
policy_desc_models_external_http: When off, a run that uses a network-capable block is refused at submit time (the runner also strips fetch).
